import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the lead's report is done; now reading the image agent's diagram manifest.

Source and manifest check out (status ready, one diagram, source matches). Checking the infographic and image links before drafting.

All three external URLs return 200 and every relative image resolves. Writing the published report now.

Validating: diagram byte-identity, anchors, links, tables, and the opening order.

Every remaining difference is intentional: heading numbers removed, `§` cross-references turned into anchor links, and one bold label promoted to a heading. Registering the artifact.

Registration worked. Last step is the final declaration.

I published the lead's report as `202611/period_strip_two_chart_redesign/period_strip_two_chart_redesign.md` in the research repo and registered it. Its reference is `research:202611/period_strip_two_chart_redesign/period_strip_two_chart_redesign.md` (`file:explicit:7db8fa570c16a35616f54407`). The commit is declared, and the host makes it after this turn ends.

**Opening order:** the file starts with the title, then a short research-query blockquote, then the infographic (`period_strip_two_chart_redesign_infographic.png`, which exists beside the report), then `## Bottom line`.

**How I restructured it:**
- **Headings:** I removed the lead's hand-numbered headings ("1." through "10.", "6.1" through "6.7"), because the PDF renderer numbers sections itself. Punctuation came out of headings that are link targets. The lead's "(verified)", "(my changes, called out)" and "Critique:" now sit in each section's first line.
- **Cross-references:** each `§N` became an in-document link to the matching section. Point 3 under "What the data says", A5, and the open-questions section are linked by name.
- **Section order:** "Where the reports disagreed and how I resolved it" moved to after the implementation plan. Otherwise the lead's order is kept, ending with "Recommended solution" and then "Sources and method".
- **Lead's preamble:** the italic paragraph (date, the commits checked, the method) moved to the start of "Sources and method", since nothing may sit between the title, query, infographic and bottom line.
- **Content:** I kept every claim, caveat, table cell, code block, figure and caption. Every line that differs from the lead's was checked by diff, and only headings and cross-references changed.

**Diagrams:** the image agent's status was `ready` and its manifest's `source` matched the lead's label.
- Accepted: `switch-ownership` → `#figure-switch-ownership`. The diagram's anchor text is in a list item under "The switch", so the figure follows that whole list. A one-sentence reference paragraph sits directly above it. The fence is byte-identical to the manifest.
- None omitted.

**Checks:**
- Every in-document anchor resolves in `pandoc -t html`, including `id="figure-switch-ownership"`.
- There is exactly one `<div id="figure-` wrapper.
- There is one Mermaid fence: the lead had none, plus the one accepted diagram.
- All four relative image links resolve from the report folder.
- All three external URLs (ONS bar charts, ONS stacked bar charts, W3C non-text contrast) returned 200, and they match the lead's URL set exactly.
- Nothing was unrepairable.
